verdict.summary: Round 5 confirms the prior approval. The selector remains fail-closed: only eligible .github YAML paths can reach the carve-out, and they are skipped only when both revisions are readable, every non-comment line is verbatim-identical, and PyYAML parses both documents to equal structures. This conservatively rejects code edits, trailing-comment changes, malformed or missing blobs, YAML normalization mismatches, and comment or blank-line edits that change block-scalar content. The real path uses the same merge base as the three-dot changed-path diff; failures disable the optimization or force the existing full-run behavior. Selection wiring preserves independent crate changes and unrelated full triggers. The tests exercise both proof halves, fail-closed cases, actual divergent-history blob resolution, memoization, audit rendering, and mixed-path selection, with meaningful negative controls. This is consistent with the change-selection design's proof-of-non-interference invariant. No correctness, soundness, security, or test-validity issue was found.
